reading.body:
A single OpenStreetMap way in Dueville, Italy is tagged as a data center under the name "Set," and nothing in the record identifies who operates it or how much power it draws.

The entry carries no capacity figure, no operator, no website, and no business registration. Its only source is an OpenStreetMap tagging review dated 2026-09-04, and the research note states that search quota ran out before the name could be resolved. "Set" is short and generic, and the record itself acknowledges it could be an abbreviation, an acronym, or a fragment of a longer name.

For AI infrastructure, the useful signal is the location rather than the facility. Dueville sits in the Veneto region near Vicenza, an area of light industry and small technology firms, and the nearest listed airport is Padova Gino Allegri Airfield about 21.6 miles away. That is consistent with a small regional facility, not with the large, power-hungry campuses that anchor AI training. The data does not establish which it is.

What this does not tell a reader is nearly everything that would matter for a compute assessment: installed capacity in megawatts, grid connection, cooling, ownership, or whether the site is even operational. It is one unverified point on a map, and it should be read as a candidate for further checking rather than as a confirmed data center.
